Subject: Objective judgement pack: calibration & rationale

Team —

Attached is the first pass of the Objective Judgement Pack for the quarter. I pulled the raw scores from the tracking sheet, added my annotations where there were obvious divergence signals, and included a short narrative draft for the QBR appendix (attached as narrative-draft.md).

As a reminder, what I need from you today:
- Vivek: line-by-line scoring rationale for infra & runtime objectives (flag anything you want escalated).
- Laura: review product-facing objectives and call out any customer-facing evidence that should adjust scores.
- Marissa: confirm the cross-functional evidence bullets for CS and Sales.
- Grace: overall leadership call — do you want any objectives treated as escalations to exec review?

I scheduled a 30-min calibration slot at 3pm PT to lock final scores and short justifications for the QBR slides. If you cannot make it, post your final adjustments in the sheet and I will capture the rationale.

Attachments: 20261118-score_spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx, 1.2MB), 20261118-heatmap.png (png, 420KB), 20261118-narrative-draft.md (text)

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Objective judgement pack: calibration & rationale

Jonas —

Thanks for pulling this together. I went through the infra/runtime rows and made a few adjustments in the spreadsheet:
- Reduced infra availability score from 95 -> 90: we had two transient incidents that were within SLA but show risk pattern because autorecover failed twice on the same node pool.
- Increased inference-cost-efficiency from 70 -> 75 after accounting for the batching pilot results in Oct (see comment on row 8).

Inline notes on the sheet explain the evidence. For the narrative, suggested language to explain the downgrade: "Availability remains within SLA but repeat node-pool failures exposed an operational fragility we are remediating through kernel rollback and targeted smoke tests."

I attached the updated spreadsheet (20261118-score_spreadsheet.xlsx) and left cell-level comments where I expect discussion.

On scheduling: I can make 3pm but may need to drop after 15 minutes; if we need deeper debate we should push an extra 45-min follow-up.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Inference Platform
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Jonas / Vivek —

Thanks for the updates. Quick note on the Product OKRs:
- Customer onboarding speed: I pushed the score down from 85 -> 78 based on the anonymized onboarding timelines Marissa shared (average slipped by 6 days this quarter). I added evidence in the sheet (column H) linking to two customer playbooks and the onboarding timeline export.
- Feature adoption (search ranking improvements): I left the score at 82 but added a moderate-risk flag — adoption increased but not at the target cohort size, and the funnel shows weaker retention beyond week 1.

One ask: can we surface the customer quotes in the narrative? Sara at Acme flagged a line that will be useful for the QBR audience: "integration made retrieval feel immediate — but we still saw edge cases on long-context retrieval." If Grace wants to highlight customer voice, we should include that quote.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management

Reviewed. I sign off on the proposed scores and the narrative language with two small asks:
1) Add a single-slide "next steps" that maps owners + timelines for the remediation items (Vivek to own kernel rollback; Marissa to own customer outreach plan).
2) Add a one-line mitigation next to each "watch" objective so execs see action not just signal.

No need to escalate to exec review — we'll present as-is and use the one-slide next steps to show we have a plan. Jonas, please finalize and send to the exec deck owner by EOD tomorrow.
